newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus hopes for military plane revived.
newsitem.headline: Airbus hopes for military plane revived.

text.p: European aircraft consortium Airbus Industrie said on Wednesday it would go ahead and create a new military arm after European governments revived plans to order the FLA new military transporter aircraft.

Andy Lewis, Airbus commercial director for FLA, said senior defence procurement officials from eight European nations met at the Paris air show yesterday to invite FLA industry partners to prepare their bid to develop and build up to 291 aircraft.

"It (the bid) will be a fixed price for development and production aircraft... specifications, contract terms and conditions and everything that will enable us to then negotiate a contract with them (prospective government customers)."

The multi-billion dollar Future Large Aircraft (FLA) project was conceived by the European industry to challenge U.S. firm Lockheed Martin's dominance of the market for tactical transport aircraft with its Hercules C130s.

But lack of development funds from member governments has compelled the pan-European consortium to treat the project like a commercial aircraft project, to be managed by Airbus and with funding based on winning a launch order.

"Over the next few weeks we will agree with our partners and shareholders the final details of our organisation and prepare to commence work on the proposal," said Alain Flourens, who is to be president of Airbus Military.

France, Germany, Italy, Spain and Turkey all gave their immediate go-ahead on Tuesday to making the official Request for Proposal (RFP), while Britain is expected to join shortly, once the new Labour government has had time to consider it.
"The Request For Proposal means that the industry can get on with the detailed proposal for 291 aircraft for the eight nations," Lewis told Reuters.
"We were really pleased that we were able to do this at the show...It's a big step forward in this programme."
Lewis said Britain was represented at Tuesday's meeting by the Ministry of Defence's senior aircraft procurement official Ian Fawcett, who promised a decision by his government by September.

The previous Conservative government said it would buy the FLA if the project was put on a commercial footing, the price was right and it was available when it comes round to replacing the rest of its ageing fleet of Hercules C130H aircraft.

Lewis said initial production for the FLA was likely to be around 270 aircraft for six countries including Britain but that number would go up to 291 aircraft if Belgium and Portugal also joined the contract negotiations. Both countries were represented at yesterday's meeting as observers, he said.

Members of the FLA industrial consortium include Airbus partners Aerospatiale, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, British Aerospace Plc, and Spain's Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (Casa) as well as Finmeccanica of Italy's Alenia unit.
